source.title: Emergence of Phonemic, Syntactic, and Semantic Representations in Artificial Neural Networks
source.authors: P. Orhan; Pablo J. Diego-Sim'on; Emmnanuel Chemla; Yair Lakretz; Yves Boubenec; Jean-Rémi King

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures how individual models encode phonemic, lexical-semantic, and syntactic structures, including changes with model size and training. It does not measure similarity between independently trained models on shared inputs, so it neither tests nor uses the convergence claim. It cites the Platonic Representation Hypothesis.
record.gate_note: The reported probe scores measure how well a model's activation geometry matches linguistic target structures, not whether distances from different models become more alike. Those results are recorded as findings about a related but different construct; cited results from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study fits linear structural probes so that one model's activation distances match linguistic target distances (articulatory, WordNet path, dependency tree). It never compares representations between models on shared inputs. Score rises with size measure alignment to a linguistic structure, not between models, so it neither tests nor uses any version. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (Huh et al. 2024) is cited only in the discussion, as one of several works on geometric laws.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. More precisely, the authors conclude that speech and text models build linear subspaces encoding phonemic, lexical-semantic and syntactic structure. In audio models these emerge in sequence (phonemes, then partial semantics, then syntax). The models need 2–4 orders of magnitude more data than children. Conclusions concern representation, not inference.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses linear structural probes to compare activation-space distances with linguistic target distances; it does not implement a method for measuring alignment between independently trained models.
record.method_sensitivity: Probe objective and evaluation metric affect quantitative scores. The authors report different quantitative outcomes for distance-based and contrastive probes, and poorer syntactic and semantic scores when using NeMo rather than Montreal Forced Aligner alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Phonemic articulatory probe scores reach 0.75 in English Wav2Vec 2.0, against 0.2 for the untrained checkpoint. Scores rise from tiny to base to large, and are low for French, music and environmental-sound models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Probe-accessible phonemic structure in speech models grows with model size and depends on speech-specific pretraining.

fits_no_version.finding: WordNet semantic probe scores rise across the Pythia suite (0.118 to 0.29) and plateau for Llama 2 (0.42 at 7B, 0.415 at 13B). Audio models score lower, and control audio models score in a similar range to English audio models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Probe-accessible lexical-semantic structure rises with text-model size and plateaus; in audio models it largely reflects acoustic cues.

fits_no_version.finding: Syntactic probe scores are 0.76 (Wav2Vec 94M), 0.81 (Pythia 1.4B) and 0.82 (Llama2 13B), rising and then plateauing with size. In control audio models, high scores reflect a linear-tree confound.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dependency-tree distance structure is linearly recoverable across speech and text models, and plateaus with size.

record.problems: The study reports aggregate probe scores and does not directly test cross-model alignment. Its main evidence is structural probing rather than prediction-based evaluation; the authors note that their distance choices may be restrictive, the analysis is limited to nouns for semantics, and forced-alignment errors make audio results lower-bound estimates. Some scaling results are presented in figures without exact values.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for the phonemic and syntactic checkpoint trajectories, alternate contrastive-probe curves, or phonemic data controls were added: these report probe-score trends or controls for individual-model linguistic structure, not convergence between models. Their qualitative findings are summarized in fits_no_version. Figure-only point values and supplementary category-level results were also omitted.

untested.parts: All: no alignment between independently trained models is measured.
All: no vision–language pairs. The paired text/speech benchmark is used only to probe each model separately.
All: no cross-model mapping or stitching. The probes map model activations to linguistic targets, not one model onto another.
All: the single-unit analyses are within one Llama2-13B model only.
All: the metric dependence reported (distance vs contrastive probe; MFA vs NeMo aligner) concerns probe scores, not cross-model convergence.
All: the reported plateaus are in probe scores, not in cross-model alignment.

record.verdict_notes: Verdict: not a test of representation convergence (T6, cites_only). The paper cites the Platonic Representation Hypothesis only in passing. The only 'alignment' computed is between the semantic and syntactic probe subspaces within Llama2-13B (max 0.042), which is within-model, not cross-model. The text also labels Figure 3C's Wav2Vec model as 160M, inconsistent with the 94M given elsewhere.

versions.untested_parts: Alignment between independently trained models, and whether that alignment rises with model size or capability.
Cross-modal alignment between vision and language models on paired images and captions.
Shared features or subspaces across independently initialized networks of the same architecture.
Mapping or stitching representations between models, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
Metric, setting, and input dependence of measured cross-model convergence.
Whether cross-model alignment is incomplete or plateaus, and whether shared data or objectives explain it.

rows.subject: Wav2Vec 2.0 English speech model

rows.measure: Spearman correlation between probe-space distances and articulatory distances
rows.note: This evaluates one model against linguistic distances, not alignment between models.
rows.check: Within-model probe score against articulatory distances; no cross-model measure. The record has the baseline right (random checkpoint 0.2).
